detail.body:
# Description

Reduce host overhead in the fused MXFP8 grouped MLP (`GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMGLU`), forward and backward, by passing operands to the cuDNN frontend grouped GEMM wrappers in their natural layouts.

cuDNN frontend `develop` lets the grouped GEMM wrappers take A as `(sum(m), k)`, B as `(num_groups, n, k)`, 1-D probabilities and the packed scale buffers as-is, and return 2-D outputs: NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1233 for the forward GLU and quant wrappers, NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1422 for the backward dGLU, dgrad (quant) and wgrad wrappers. Today TE builds 3-D/6-D views of every operand on each call, and the frontend maps them back.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- **Forward:** when the GLU and quant wrappers advertise `supports_canonical_layouts`, the MXFP8 forward passes canonical A/B/probability/scale operands and consumes the 2-D C/D and packed SFD outputs directly, without per-call view/permute chains.
- **FC2 amax:** FC2 skips its unused output amax when the quant wrapper advertises `supports_optional_amax`.
- **Backward dGLU:** when the dGLU wrapper also advertises `supports_canonical_layouts`, the MXFP8 backward passes:
  - 2-D grad output and activation input;
  - 1-D probabilities and dprob;
  - packed scale buffers as-is;
  - the FC2 column-wise weight as `(num_groups, k, n)` with `b_major="n"`.

  The 2-D dGLU outputs are used directly.
- **Backward FC1 dgrad:** uses the 2-D dGLU outputs, the FC1 column-wise weight with `b_major="n"`, and a 2-D grad input.
- **Backward wgrad:** passes flat scale buffers when the wgrad wrapper supports them.
- **Unchanged:** NVFP4, SReLU, and frontends without these attributes keep the existing path. The forward and backward are gated separately, so a frontend with only NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1233 still gets the forward change.
- **Docs:** the fused op docstring notes the layout behavior.

## Measurements

Host p50 in µs, median of three interleaved rounds, on this branch rebased on `main` at 459dedc.

Per forward:

| Configuration | Host p50 | End-to-end p50 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `main` | 458.0 | 470.4 |
| This PR | 360.7 | 374.2 |

Per forward + backward step:

| Configuration | Host p50 |
|---|---:|
| `main` | 1500 |
| Canonical forward only | 1416 |
| This PR (forward and backward) | 1346 |

**Setup:**
- Hardware and stack: SM100, TE built from this branch (sm_100), cuDNN frontend with NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1233 and NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1422, CuTeDSL 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0a0.
- Workload: an isolated 4096-row, 8-expert MLP with hidden size 2048 and intermediate size 512, MXFP8 weights, BF16 input and probabilities, `ScaledSwiGLU(glu_interleave_size=32)`, gradients enabled.
- Method: pinned CPU, 300 synchronized samples per process, configurations interleaved over three rounds.

## Testing

- `tests/pytorch/test_grouped_mlp.py`, merged with `main` at dfc4158 (cuDNN FE 1.32.0, canonical layouts on): 1252 passed, 3986 skipped, 0 failed.
- The forward output, input and probability gradients, and both weight gradients are bitwise identical to `main`.

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

inline_comments.body:
Done for the weight views in 76581d8. The typed `(groups, n, k)` view of each weight buffer is now built once and kept on the grouped weight. It is rebuilt only if the buffer's data pointer changes. This covers all four sites: FC1 and FC2 in the forward, and the FC2 dGLU and FC1 dgrad in the backward. Each site drops from two torch ops (1.6 µs) to 0.24 µs.

The remaining `view(dtype=...)` calls are on buffers that are new every step: the quantized activations and the freshly swizzled weight scales. Each costs about 0.6 µs. TE stores quantized data as `uint8` and cuDNN takes the FP8/FP4 dtype, so dropping those needs one of two changes:
- the TE quantizers allocate typed storage, or
- the cuDNN frontend accepts raw `uint8` MXFP8 buffers with a dtype hint.

I can do the cuDNN side as a follow-up.

I think the dtype mismatch causing cpu overhead should've been avoided. In TE mxfp8 tensor, the storage dtype is uint8 with a TE metadata tracking if it's E4M2 or E5M2, I think TE has been doing this for years already. 

I am also generally against having too many version gates in TE about cudnn-fe versions, so if you do plan to change cudnn-fe API, I think you can just increase the version gate of cudnn-fe's canonical layout version gate as a whole, otherwise under canonical layout, we will have to check cudnn-fe again and divide up further. 

I am even open to increase cudnn-fe version gate once for all in TE and drop the older cudnn-fe support so that we have canonical layout only, but that's up to @timmoon10 @vthumbe1503 to decide :)

Local test results across cuDNN frontend versions, since TE CI ships FE 1.29 and does not exercise the canonical-layout path.

Tested at 4ad153e (before the final merge with `main` in ca511f5). `tests/pytorch/test_grouped_mlp.py` (5238 tests) on SM100, cuDNN 9.25.1, CUDA 13.4, torch 2.14.0a0 (NGC 26.08), CuTeDSL 4.7.1. Only the frontend version changes between rows.

| cuDNN FE | Path | Passed | Skipped | Failed | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.26.0 | fused op unavailable | 1185 | 4045 | 0 | 8 |
| 1.28.0 | legacy layouts | 1246 | 3992 | 0 | 0 |
| 1.29.1 (TE CI) | legacy layouts | 1252 | 3986 | 0 | 0 |
| 1.30.0 | legacy layouts | 1251 | 3987 | 0 | 0 |
| 1.31.0 | canonical forward, legacy backward | 1252 | 3986 | 0 | 0 |
| 1.32.0 | canonical forward and backward | 1252 | 3986 | 0 | 0 |
| 1.32.1 | canonical forward and backward | 1252 | 3986 | 0 | 0 |

Differences from 1.29.1:
- 1.26.0: the 8 errors are FE 1.26 failing to import under CuTeDSL 4.7.1 (`ReduxKind` is missing from `cutlass._mlir.dialects.nvvm`), in the frontend's own `grouped_gemm_quant` import. They hit the setup of `test_grouped_mlp_glu_mxfp8_real_cudnn_fusion` (6) and `test_grouped_mlp_situglu_nvfp4_real_cudnn_hadamard_fusion` (2). The extra skips come from the fused op being unsupported.
- 1.28.0: the five `test_grouped_mlp_activation_recompute[*-scaled_tanh_srelu-*]` tests skip because that kernel is not in 1.28.
- 1.28.0 and 1.30.0: `test_dprob_is_bit_exact_across_runs[scaled_swiglu-GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMGLU]` skips because the dGLU wrapper in those versions does not accept `deterministic`.
